headline: High: Plandex can read/write and execute shell by default, while Pathway has no direct I/O, so the main risks are B/C/D from the pairwise workflow rather than prompt injection.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway has no filesystem, clipboard, stdin/stdout, MCP, or browser surfaces, so there is no documented channel for its outputs to directly inject instructions into Plandex. Plandex can read files and use stdin/stdout, but without a shared bridge from Pathway the pairwise injection pathway is not present.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, re-evaluate for injection.
IF Pathway begins emitting content that Plandex parses as instructions, the severity increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any copy-paste or file handoff between them.
Require explicit human review before Plandex consumes Pathway output.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pathway is documented as not reading or writing files and touching no data classes, while Plandex reads and writes a project directory and handles source code plus model-provider API keys. The pairwise leakage path is limited because Pathway has no documented sensitive-data surface, but Plandex can still expose whatever it ingests if the operator bridges them.
conditions: IF Pathway is connected to a shared workspace containing secrets or regulated data, leakage risk increases.
IF Plandex is pointed at files produced by Pathway that contain sensitive content, those contents may flow to its backend.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the shared project directory.
Use separate directories for each agent.
Redact sensitive fields before handing Pathway output to Plandex.
Review Plandex inputs before any cloud/model-provider call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pathway cannot write files or modify git state, but Plandex can write the filesystem, modify git state, and execute shell commands. The overlap is asymmetric rather than mutually conflicting, yet Plandex's default write and git capabilities can still race with any external process that consumes Pathway outputs, so uncertainty favors medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable repository, concurrent edits can collide.
IF an orchestrator copies Pathway outputs into Plandex-managed files without locking, write conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate directory.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Disable auto-apply in Plandex during shared edits.
Use git branches per agent and merge manually.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pathway is a document-processing agent with no direct action surface, while Plandex is a coding agent with review-then-apply and optional auto-apply. If Pathway's output is treated as authoritative input to Plandex, errors can cascade into code changes or shell actions; the pairwise workflow is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Pathway output is fed into Plandex without verification, downstream mistakes can be applied.
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled, erroneous upstream content can become committed changes.
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents.
Add schema validation for Pathway outputs.
Block shell execution for tasks derived from Pathway results.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is documented in either profile: Pathway has no touched data classes and Plandex only lists source code plus model-provider API keys. Without evidence of regulated data residency, retention, or certification differences, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, compliance must be reassessed.
IF one agent is deployed under a stricter residency or retention policy than the other, mismatch risk may appear.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Verify deployment region before processing sensitive data.
